title: Claim: n0n ransomware gang says it leaked Samsung smart TV viewing and political ad data
date_note: Technext's publication day (its feed gives 19 November 2026); the article gives no date for the leak itself. The viewing records are described as from 2024.
place: South Korea (company's home country as the article states)
geo_basis: country as stated ('South Korean tech giant'); no city given
summary: Technext, citing Cybernews researchers who examined the files, reports that a ransomware gang called n0n has allegedly dumped 220MB of data from an alleged Samsung Electronics breach on its leak site. Per Technext, the largest dataset holds about 150,000 smart TV viewing events from 2024, alongside political advertising and AI ad-training records. Samsung had yet to comment on the claim, Technext says.
plain: A ransomware gang says it leaked Samsung data, including about 150,000 smart TV viewing records from 2024. Samsung has not commented and the claim is unconfirmed.
exec: Unconfirmed extortion claim against Samsung involving smart TV viewing and ad data; no company confirmation.
impact: Unconfirmed; Technext says the records do not reveal what individual users watched.

evidence.quote: The largest dataset holds about 150,000 smart TV viewing events from 2024.
A ransomware gang called n0n has allegedly dumped 220MB of the data on the dark web.

validation.note: Attacker's claim relayed by Technext from Cybernews; the Cybernews original answered 403 and was not read. No Samsung statement found; Technext says Samsung had yet to comment.

report.note: Technext article read in full; it relays Cybernews.
